notes.togenda: Pe with i- tells one person not to do it.

guidebook.intro: Saying no is easy in Acholi: put **pe** in front.

tips.title: Pe: not
body: **Pe** before the verb makes it negative: **Pe amito kawa** (I don’t want coffee), **Pe angeyo** (I don’t know), **Pe aniang** (I don’t understand). On its own, **Pe** means “no”.
**Pe atye ki** is “I don’t have”: **Pe atye ki cente** (I have no money).

tips.title: Pe icit! Don’t go!
body: To tell someone not to do something, use **pe** with **i-**: **Pe icit!** (don’t go!), **Pe ilwor** (don’t be afraid), **Pe ikok** (don’t cry).
**Pud** means still or not yet: **Pud pe acamo** (I haven’t eaten yet).

culture.title: A soft no
body: A blunt no can sound rude. People soften it: **Pe, apwoyo** (no, thank you), or **Twero bedo diki** (maybe tomorrow).
